summary: Storefront evidence for CFM grouped catalog canary (3 products x 11 foreign markets), measured against today's production build. Every cell serves the real product under its CFM-authored translated slug, in the market's exact locale, at the channel price, not purchasable, not indexable. Slovakia unchanged.

measured_against.host: maky.store — PM2 app maky-storefront (next start -p 3000 behind nginx) on ubuntu@ip-10-0-2-88
measured_against.probe_origin: http://127.0.0.1:3000 (the rollback gate origin; the public URL is the same artifact behind nginx)
measured_against.note: This supersedes M_CATALOG_PATCH_DEPLOYED.json as the deploy reference: production has moved on twice since 5ce2f0b. Evidence is bound to the SHA above, not to a historical M deploy.

cfm_binding._comment: Delivered by CFM 2026-09-21 and copied verbatim. The CFM artifact tree lives on a different host — /home/ubuntu/cfm-artifacts/ does not exist here — so M cannot recompute these hashes and does not claim to have verified them. What M verified is in `checks`, which is measured against the live storefront and Saleor and needs none of these values.
cfm_binding.code_pin_note: CFM reported 2026-09-21 that the release named by $GO (tip 8c5c37c, release commerce-2-8c5c37cfb253) does NOT match the code pin the canary wrote into its journal — grouped_l10n.py and nordrive_l10n/journal.py differ. The canary ran from a release matching seven others, including commerce-2-current (f23439aa), and CFM ran the schema-only gate from that one. Recorded here so the evidence chain names the code that actually produced the canary, not the one the GO names. CFM-reported, not verifiable from this host.
cfm_binding.canary_run_id_note: Not an independent identifier — it is the string `market_catalog_grouped-` plus the first 12 characters of grouped_plan_sha256, so it names the plan, not a particular execution of it.

cfm_reported.source: CFM session report, not independently verifiable from the storefront

scope.note: These are the three products CFM's grouped canary published on 2026-09-19 — not a historical canary set. Every foreign channel holds exactly these three and nothing else.

real_product_not_soft_404.how: JSON-LD @type Product had to be present AND its name had to equal the Saleor translation name for that exact language code. HTTP 200 alone is not evidence — the not-found page also answers 200.

identity_matches_cfm_product_id.how: Cell resolved from Saleor by externalReference cfm:product:<id>; the served page's JSON-LD name compared against that product's translation(languageCode) name.

final_translated_slug.how: URL built from Saleor translation slug; canonical had to echo it.

not_purchasable.how: Saleor isAvailableForPurchase=false in all 11 foreign channels; the PDP renders it as schema.org/OutOfStock and the sold-out label.

history_url_one_301_to_final.note: 36, not 33: the map carries three extra HU rows for the intermediate slugs the canary passed through. All resolve in a single hop to the final slug.

gates_at_measurement.indexable_markets_note: MAKY_INDEXABLE_MARKETS is not present in .env; the effective value comes from the code default (['sk'] intersected with MAKY_LIVE_MARKETS). Turning on more markets needs the variable AND a rebuild — hreflang for static pages is baked at build time.

not_claimed: Nothing here proves the other 9154 products of the cohort. Each foreign channel holds exactly 3 published products; the rest are unpublished and every other foreign product URL renders the localized not-found page (HTTP 200, noindex) in both its old and its new slug form.
CFM's own counters (mutation executions, readback hashes, plan SHA) are reproduced as reported, not verified — the storefront cannot see them.
JSON-LD brand is null on every cell. Pre-existing CFM data gap (cfm:attribute:manufacturer), unrelated to this rollout.
